# Collect Google Cloud Audit Logs

**Parser Version:** 38.0

Supported in:

Google SecOps  [ SIEM ](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/secops/google-secops-siem-toc)

This document describes how you can export Cloud Audit Logs by enabling Google Cloud telemetry ingestion to Google Security Operations and how Cloud Audit Logs fields map to Google Security Operations Unified Data Model (UDM) fields.

For more information, see [Data ingestion to Google Security Operations overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/data-ingestion-flow).

A typical deployment consists of Cloud Audit Logs enabled for ingestion to Google Security Operations. Each customer deployment might differ from this representation and might be more complex.

The deployment contains the following components:

  * **Google Cloud** : The Google Cloud services and products from which you collect logs

  * **Cloud Audit Logs** : The Cloud Audit Logs that are enabled for ingestion to Google Security Operations

  * **Google Workspace audit logs** : The Google Workspace audit logs that are enabled for ingestion to Google Security Operations

  * **Google Security Operations** : Retains and analyzes Cloud Audit Logs and Google Workspace audit logs




An ingestion label identifies the parser which normalizes raw log data to structured UDM format. The information in this document applies to the parser with `GCP_CLOUDAUDIT` ingestion label. 

## Before you begin

  * Ensure that you have set up a [Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/enterprise/setup-checklist).
  * Ensure that you have set up access control for your organization and resources using Identity and Access Management (IAM). For more information about access control, see [Access control for organizations with IAM](https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/access-control-org). 

  * [Configure data access audit logs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/audit/configure-data-access#configuration_overview) for your Google Cloud resources and services.

  * Ensure that all systems in the deployment architecture are configured in the UTC time zone.

  * Verify the log types that the Cloud Audit Logs parser supports. The following table lists the log sources and types supported by the Cloud Audit Logs parser:

## Configure ingestion of Cloud Audit Logs

To ingest Cloud Audit Logs to Google Security Operations, follow the steps on the [Ingest Google Cloud logs to Google Security Operations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/ingestion/cloud/ingest-gcp-logs) page.

**Caution:** Data Access logs written by Cloud Audit Logs can produce a large volume of data that has low value for threat detection. The volume might result in data-throttling due to the enforcement of [burst limits](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/ingestion/burst-limits). To learn how to filter out logs that are generated by routine activities, see [Tune Cloud Audit Logs filters](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/ingestion/default-parsers/ingest-gcp-logs#tune-audit-filters).

If you encounter issues when you ingest Cloud Audit Logs, [contact Google Security Operations support](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/support).

## Supported Cloud Audit Logs log formats

The Cloud Audit Logs parser supports logs in JSON format.

## Field mapping reference

This section explains how the Google Security Operations parser maps Cloud Audit Logs fields to Google Security Operations Unified Data Model (UDM) fields.

### Field mapping reference: GCP_CLOUDAUDIT log types to UDM event type

The following table lists the `GCP_CLOUDAUDIT` event identifiers (from the `protoPayload.methodName` raw log field) and their corresponding UDM event types.

**Note:** Because `GCP_CLOUDAUDIT` covers a vast number of Google Cloud services and API methods, listing every individual method mapping is not feasible. The following table lists the most common explicit method-to-event-type mappings by service. For methods not explicitly listed, the parser uses regular expression pattern matching on the method name to assign an appropriate UDM event type instead of defaulting to `GENERIC_EVENT`.

---|---

### Fallback additional.fields mapping

When multiple candidate raw log fields map to the same single-value UDM field, the `GCP_CLOUDAUDIT` parser evaluates those fields in the priority order defined in the Field mapping reference: GCP_CLOUDAUDIT - Common Fields section. If a raw log contains non-empty values for more than one candidate field, the highest-priority value populates the target **Primary UDM field** , and any remaining non-empty candidate values are preserved in `additional.fields` so that no audit context is lost.

The following table lists each fallback `additional.fields` key (**Fallback UDM mapping**), the source raw log field (**Log field**), and the target UDM field that triggers the fallback (**Primary UDM field**).

## UDM Mapping Delta

**Note:** In this delta, "Old UDM Mapping" refers to releases before 23rd October, 2026. Versions released after 23rd October, 2026 include the following "New UDM Mapping".**Note:** All deprecated fields—`about.labels`, `intermediary.labels`, `observer.labels`, `principal.labels`, `src.labels`, `security_result.about.labels`, and `target.labels`—have been removed from the mapping.
